name: Scope and time
summary: Preferences have a scope (a project, a context) and a lifetime (today, this month, until further notice). EV must not let a local or temporary preference leak into everything forever.

scenarios.title: Project-scoped tone does not bleed
scenarios.guards: Over-generalising a preference from one project to all

steps.say: For the Slow Bread bakery client website, keep all copy warm but formal, no slang, no emojis.
steps.memory: Formal/no-emoji tone scoped to the Slow Bread project, not global.

steps.say: For my YouTube devlog, I want the opposite: casual, jokey, emojis fine.
steps.memory: Casual tone scoped to the devlog.

steps.say: write the 'about us' paragraph for the bakery site
now write the description for my next devlog video about adding streaks to Tidepool
write a LinkedIn post about Tidepool
expect: Picks a sensible middle or asks which tone; does not blindly apply either project's rule.

scenarios.title: Temporary situation expires
scenarios.guards: A temporary constraint becoming a permanent trait

steps.say: I'm travelling for the next two weeks and only have my phone, so keep anything you give me phone-friendly
steps.memory: Phone-only constraint with an end date about two weeks out.

steps.say: give me a quick plan for adding reminders to Tidepool
expect: Short, phone-readable; no wide tables or big code blocks.

steps.say: give me a detailed implementation plan for reminders in Tidepool
expect: Full detail; no phone-only restriction applied.
Optionally checks: 'are you back from your trip?'
fail: Still compresses for a phone without asking.

scenarios.title: Exception beats the rule, only where it applies
scenarios.guards: An exception overwriting the general rule

steps.say: In general I want TypeScript for anything I build
except data scripts, those should just be Python
steps.memory: General rule TypeScript; exception: data scripts in Python. Both active.

steps.say: write a small script that reads my Tidepool habits CSV export and prints weekly completion %
now a tiny web page that shows those numbers
fail: Python for the web page because the last task was Python.

scenarios.title: Mood is not a preference
scenarios.guards: Learning permanent traits from one bad day

steps.say: ugh just give me the answer, no explanation, I'm so done today. how do I undo the last git commit but keep the changes
steps.memory: At most a low-confidence, today-scoped note. No permanent 'never explain' rule.

steps.say: how does git rebase actually work under the hood?
expect: A real explanation; the question asks for depth.

steps.say: for this month don't factor in that I'm vegetarian, I'm doing a protein experiment with my doctor
steps.memory: Vegetarian claim kept but paused (stop-use with expiry), not erased.

fail: Vegetarian fact lost because the pause was treated as erase.
